messages:
maya: FYI — customer reported our JS SDK broke in their Cloudflare Worker sample app after last publish.
alex: Ow. Error?
maya: `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: (0 , _inference.default) is not a function` when doing `import inference from '@redwood/inference'`
sam: Cloudflare is ESM-only so this usually means our exported shape didn't match the ESM build. Are they using default import specifically?
maya: yep, default import. Their code is the quickstart app.
tia: we ship both CJS and ESM but I remember we changed the conditional exports mapping last quarter to favour esm for `import`. Maybe we accidentally removed a default export in the esm bundle.
alex: quick history: we produce two outputs under dist/esm and dist/cjs. package.json had `exports` pointing "import" -> ./dist/esm/index.mjs and "require" -> ./dist/cjs/index.js. We also published a transpiled commonjs that added `module.exports = { default: ... }` shim previously.
ben: bundlers and runtimes disagree on default vs named interop. Node's ESM->CJS default interop and native ESM expect `export default`. If our ESM build exports named exports only, `import default` will be undefined.
maya: Right — the quickstart used `import inference from '@redwood/inference'` which worked before.
sam: Edge runtimes (CF Workers, Deno) are more strict. Deno will fail if there's no top-level default export when you import default.
tia: Proposed path: adopt ESM-first build (clean, explicit `export default createClient`) and ship a tiny CJS compatibility wrapper for older Node consumers. That avoids runtime surprises in edge environments.
alex: Agree, but our release checklist must ensure both shapes. Also need to update `exports` to include an `edge`/`worker` condition so the runtime picks the right file: e.g. "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "worker": "./dist/edge/index.mjs" } }
ben: Also types: we need a single `types` entry that points to the ESM typings. Some consumers rely on `types` at package root instead of `exports.types` — include both to be safe.
sam: Edge note: Cloudflare's bundler will prefer the `worker` condition if present. If there's no worker condition it falls back to import — so ensure worker points to a tiny adapter that uses ESM semantics and re-exports the default.
tia: example minimal adapter for edge: ```
// dist/edge/index.mjs
import client from '../esm/index.mjs';
export default client;
export * from '../esm/index.mjs';
```
alex: And CJS shim could be `dist/cjs/index.js` -> `module.exports = require('../esm/index.mjs').default || require('../esm/index.mjs')` — but `require` can't load mjs. So we need to compile a CJS output that imports the same TS source and builds to a CJS bundle.
ben: Or produce a micro shim that re-exports precompiled CJS: `dist/cjs/index.js` compiled from TS target cjs so it's safe. We already have that in CI but maybe it wasn't published due to the export map change.
maya: Practically: customer unblock: publish a hotfix that restores a default export on the ESM build and add a smoke test for Cloudflare quickstart.
sam: I propose we add a smoke CI job that: 1) npm pack the package, 2) run a tiny Cloudflare-worker-like runner (esbuild + node's --experimental-loader?) or use `wrangler dev` CI check, 3) import default and named exports, 4) run Deno import test. Fail publishing if smoke fails.
tia: +1. Also add a test for `require('@redwood/inference')` in Node 14/16 to validate CJS semantics.
alex: Action items:
- alex: prepare ESM default export fix and edge adapter (ETA today)
- tia: add CI smoke tests for CF/Deno/Node CJS (ETA tomorrow morning)
- ben: update package.json `exports` to include `worker` and types fallbacks (ETA today)
- sam: draft a release note blurb and rollback instructions in case hotfix causes regressions (ETA today)
maya: can release-bot gate pushes until CI smoke tests pass?
release-bot: automatic: publish pipeline now requires all `smoke/cf-compat` and `smoke/deno-compat` checks to succeed before allowing npm publish.
ben: Also documentation change: quickstart should use `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'` (named import) in examples to be safer while we roll out the adapter. Update playground sample apps too.
maya: I'll open the customer-facing ticket and link quickstart PR once alex pushes the fix.
alex: pushing branch now, will open PR with tests and example changes.
sam: thanks — please @me on the PR.
tia: and create a follow-up to discuss long-term policy: ESM-first but CI-enforced CJS parity, and explicit `exports` with `worker` condition.
maya: pretty happy with that plan. :thumbsup:
ben: merging playbook into release checklist after hotfix. :+1:
alex: closing the loop here — will update when PR is ready.
